['How can we really help suicidal people?. All the responses are "reach out for help" ,"talk to someone" and that we need to do more to start talking about mental health. But what if you\'re extremely suicidal. You cant forget these are extremely personal and dark thoughts that people most likely dont want to talk to anyone about because they feel vulnerable or exposed, because they dont know how to talk about it, theres nobody to talk to or they dont want anybody to know about it. Say if someone finds the idea of death really comforting and wants to be dead. Their feelings are really dark and serious and they want to be found dead. I\'ve spoken to my school counsellor, doctor and other mental health people about my symptoms of depression and they all just seem so belittling and ask questions that indicates they\'re not taking it seriously. I wouldnt want to tell any of those people my dark feelings or how I want to die. It\'s not very realistic. You\'re not going to go up to a teacher and tell them you want to die and they\'re likely not going to care or do anything anyway. It just makes for an awkward relationship for the rest of your time at that school. These people you are supposed to talk to make me uncomfortable and I just dont want to open up. What if someone doesnt want to talk to sit in a room and awkwardly talk about their feelings, what if they want to be found dead? I\'ve used all the chatlines/hotlines in my country hundreds of times and they always are like "how does that make you feel?" , "how long has this been going on for?" ,"do you have any siblings?" And try to divert the conversation to my home life but they say it in this cheery voice which puts me off like it\'s too uncomfortable to expose my dark feelings to these random strangers who wont take me seriously. People throw the suicide hotlines at you like it will save your life. I\'ve heard many experiences of people where its basically useless. And people on tv are like we need to start a discussion around mental health and that\'s great but not realistic, like what is that going to do? I dont see how the stigma could be decreased or it will be any less awkward telling someone you literally want to kill yourself even after we\'ve had a "discussion around mental health". Like I know what they\'re trying to do and its great. But I cringe when I hear mental health youtubers telling their parents "look at me in this video when I was really unwell-I was so ill then wasnt i" or "wow I would have never been able to eat this 5 months ago!" In front of their parents- like being open and talking about mental illness just feels so weird to me. I\'m not saying what they\'re doing is wrong, it\'s great that they\'re open but it feels so awkward and too open to me, like we are taking really dark and personal struggles and just "talking" about it really openly and its such a strange concept to me. I know I certainly dont want my parents to know I\'m feeling suicidal unless I\'m already dead, whilst I\'m alive it\'s just so invasive, exposing, embarrassing, like if they found out I was suicidal and asked me a bunch of questions I swear I wouldnt look them in the eyes again I would be the most embarrassed ever. Maybe I\'m just not used to being open and its making me skeptical of getting any help in the future. I watched this documentary where some womans husband killed himself and the wife called the ambulance and police but he already died before they got there. The police in the car was saying "if only he reached out, we could have saved him". Like, I just dont get it. What is talking about it going to do? Usually people dont know what to say except "sorry to hear that" or "I\'m here for you", or they\'re going through their own problems so they\'re not in a position to help, or people just get tired of you venting and being negative eventually. When something dramatic happens, people rush to the scene to act like they know you so well and oh if only they could have reached out but its actually very difficult to talk about these things or they dont have anyone. I dont like how easy people make it sound to "reach out". But even if you do, the support wont be there forever. After a while people will expect you to go back to normal again so they can go off and live their own lives again. Also, mental illness is brutal. It can make you want to be in pain, be violent, die..the idea of dying a painful death is appealing to some people. Another approach people take is telling people how much it would hurt their family, which in many cases is enough to keep them from doing it, but not taking the pain or stopping them from wanting to do it in the first place. It doesnt remove the cause of wanting to commit suicide. So they\'re stuck in a place of suffering but also not wanting their family to suffer. So that situation isnt great. This still doesnt come into consideration for every suicidal person because som people think they\'re a burden to their families, or the pain is too much to stand anymore. They dont care what their families think because they are in pain. Maybe they are tired. Maybe dont want to talk. Some people are in so much emotional pain that they just cant hang around on that waiting list for therapy. Some people have already tried therapy and medications. Some peoples situations cant be fixed. Say if someone with severe body dysmorphia is extremely distressed by their face, and the professionals say "sorry, we can\'t change your bone structure. But we can offer therapy and medication." But the patient is so distressed by their appearance they say "no I dont want that, you cant offer me what I really want." Can you really stop them?
